Laycock's remark ('Stress does not appear to be a phonemic feature in any of these languages') and his marking convention cover all c. 40 Lumi-subdistrict lists; Alu-specific content comes only from its forms being unmarked. Default 'first syllable not containing schwa' is a quality-sensitive left-edge default, so the reading is harmonised with mini1253#0 (same sentence) as weight-sensitive rather than fixed: initial syllable. | checker: Re-ran the archive.org full-text API myself (be-api.us.archive.org/fts/v1/search, identifier:sim_oceanic-linguistics_summer-1968_7_1) with three fresh phrase queries; windows returned 2026-09-20: 'only if it falls on…
new_statements.relation_note: Nothing on tone. Alu entry itself gives demographic data and typological codes '(e) Pi, SpOs' only, no phoneme inventory.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Survey-wide (all Lumi Subdistrict languages incl. Alu): stress is not phonemic; by Laycock's marking convention the default (unmarked) stress falls on the first syllable whose vowel is not schwa, and stress is written only when it falls elsewhere. All 46 Alu forms cited from this article in the TransNewGuinea re-keying are unmarked (while Elkei, Au, Ningil forms there do carry Laycock's acute marks), so every recorded Alu form has stress on its first non-schwa syllable (e.g. teralkit 'man', yampulte 'star', olanum 'good'; rakət 'arm').
new_statements.exceptions: Only the general provision that non-default stress would be marked; no marked Alu form is known. Statement hedged ('does not appear to be').
new_statements.identity_note: The article's entry 'Alu (Dia, Metru): (a) 1850 (b) Auang, Nunsi, Sikel, Weigint, Yemlu, Yuwil (E. Au CD), Muku, Wimbe, Wowil, Yerisi (W. Palei CD) (c) Yakop, Kolmen (Yuwil) (d) Lumi 7/67 (e) Pi, SpOs.' is Glottolog's diaa1238 (same villages as Laycock 1973 no. 22 = ISO dia); 'Galu (Metru, Sinagen)' (Wara, Weiki) is the sister languoid sina1269. The stress sentences are in the article's general transcription conventions and scope over every language surveyed ('any of these languages'), Alu included; they are first-hand (Laycock's own 1967 elicitation) but not Alu-specific.
